question: What is the primary goal of patient safety in reproductive health care?

options.A: Eliminating all financial costs of maternity care
options.B: Protecting mothers and newborns from preventable harm
options.C: Reducing the total number of hospital admissions
options.D: Speeding up patient discharge from the postnatal ward

explanation: Reproductive health safety specifically targets the prevention of adverse outcomes and injuries for both mother and baby throughout pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why do maternity wards carry high inherent risks compared to other hospital units?

options.A: Obstetric equipment is outdated across most healthcare facilities
options.B: Midwives and nurses rarely communicate with attending doctors
options.C: Patients in maternity units always reject standard medications
options.D: The rapid onset of obstetric emergencies requiring quick action

explanation: Childbirth and postpartum recovery can change rapidly from a normal state to a life-threatening emergency, raising clinical risk. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h1)

question: What does the risk identification phase involve in clinical settings?

options.A: Spotting potential hazards before they cause patient harm
options.B: Writing a detailed report for the federal ministry
options.C: Punishing staff members after an adverse event occurs
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of lost medical supplies

explanation: Risk identification is the initial step of finding vulnerabilities in the workflow before an actual injury takes place. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h2)

question: How does proactive risk management differ from reactive approaches?

options.A: It removes the need for nursing documentation completely
options.B: It anticipates system failures before errors happen
options.C: It ignores minor near-misses to focus on major surgeries
options.D: It relies entirely on patient complaints after discharge

explanation: Proactive management looks for weaknesses to prevent incidents, whereas reactive management only responds after harm has occurred. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h2)

question: Which condition is a leading cause of severe maternal morbidity and mortality?
explanation: Excessive bleeding after childbirth remains one of the most frequent and dangerous emergencies in maternity care. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h3)

question: A nurse notices a postpartum patient has a rapidly rising pulse and falling blood pressure. What does this suggest?

options.A: An allergic reaction to routine postnatal vitamins
options.B: A temporary anxiety spike from seeing the newborn
options.C: A normal physiological reaction to successful delivery
options.D: An early warning sign of postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Vital sign changes like tachycardia and hypotension are classic indicators of significant blood loss requiring immediate intervention. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h3)

question: What defines a near-miss in a clinical healthcare environment?

options.A: An event that did not reach the patient by chance or intervention
options.B: An equipment breakdown that delays a routine ward cleaning
options.C: A formal complaint filed by a patient's family after discharge
options.D: A surgical complication that results in permanent patient disability

explanation: A near-miss is a safety hazard or error caught just in time before any actual harm comes to the patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why is Root Cause Analysis preferred over blaming individual staff members?

options.A: It allows the hospital administration to avoid writing reports
options.B: It guarantees that nurses will never make a mistake again
options.C: It reduces the financial liability of the medical director
options.D: It uncovers underlying system failures that caused the error

explanation: Root Cause Analysis looks deeper than human error to fix the flawed systems and workflows that allowed the mistake to happen. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary characteristic of a just culture in healthcare?

options.A: Punishing every single nursing mistake with immediate dismissal
options.B: Leaving all safety decisions strictly to the hospital management
options.C: Balancing individual accountability with systemic error analysis
options.D: Ignoring minor protocol violations to maintain staff morale

explanation: A just culture supports open reporting and evaluates the system context rather than automatically punishing staff for mistakes. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h5)

question: What negative outcome occurs in a strictly punitive healthcare work environment?

options.A: Doctors and nurses collaborate more effectively on call
options.B: Staff members hide errors out of fear of punishment
options.C: Nurses complete incident reports for every minor event
options.D: Patient satisfaction scores increase across all wards

explanation: Fear of harsh blame drives mistakes underground, preventing the institution from learning and improving safety. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h5)

question: When must the surgical safety checklist be verified by the operating team?

options.C: When the patient registers at the gate
options.D: Only after the patient leaves recovery

explanation: The checklist requires a mandatory pause right before the incision to confirm crucial safety details collectively. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why is verbal confirmation among the surgical team during a checklist important?

options.A: It ensures everyone agrees on the procedure and patient identity
options.B: It replaces the need for written consent forms from the family
options.C: It allows the surgeon to delegate all nursing duties to students
options.D: It shortens the total duration of the surgical operation

explanation: Verbal verification engages all team members, reducing dangerous assumptions and preventing wrong-site errors. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which metric is commonly tracked to evaluate maternity safety outcomes?
explanation: Maternal mortality is a critical public health indicator used to measure the overall safety and quality of obstetric care. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of regular audit and feedback cycles in nursing units?

options.A: To eliminate the need for patient bedside handovers
options.B: To satisfy government tax requirements for private hospitals
options.C: To penalize nurses who have lower patient volume counts
options.D: To determine if safety interventions are effectively working

explanation: Audits provide objective data on clinical performance, showing teams what is improving and where gaps remain. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h7)
